short: A zero-density estimate across prime moduli

statements.markdown: The archive proves the statement from a mean-square estimate over prime moduli (meanSqK) and 1 a zero-density estimate (zero_density_box) for zeros with Re s > 1 − 400 , in the tradition of Bombieri [Bom65]; compare [Sie35b; Pag35] for the exceptional real zero that the second clause excludes.

lean.name: QH.meanSqK
lean.note: `meanSqK` bounds the sum of squares over candidate primes in the admissible progression for every $y\in[Y,Y^K]$, with the stated restrictions on prime divisors of the progression modulus. `stage` uses this bound to control how many candidates exceed the threshold anywhere in the window. This is the mean-square statement on a power window under the stated conditions on the moduli.

lean.name: Formalism.HermitianLattices.Ext.PrimitiveCharacterCasts.ZD.zero_density_box
lean.plain: A zero-density estimate across prime moduli
lean.note: `zero_density_box` bounds by $CQ^{1/4}$ the number of primitive characters of modulus at most $Q$ with at least one zero in $\operatorname{Re}s>1-1/400$, $|\operatorname{Im}s|\le Q$, for $Q\ge3$. The application counts bad primes by assigning each one such a character whose modulus records that prime. This declaration proves the named zero-density bound used in the exposition.
